notes: Working name Bernardia myricifolia (Scheele) S.Watson; Bernardia incana and Tyria myricifolia documented previous names.

morphology_candidate.look_here_first: Look for densely branched shrub, small crenate leaves and stellate hairs; then determine plant sex and inspect woolly 3-lobed capsule.

confusers.separator: Bernardia is dioecious; confirm flower/fruit and stellate-hair details.
Use shrub habit plus reproductive structures.

notes: Need separate diagnostic photos for sex-specific flowers and woolly capsule.

taxonomy.notes: POWO/WCVP and Flora of North America accept Bernardia myricifolia. Older reports outside its southern-Texas range have sometimes involved B. incana or B. obovata; preserve modern concept.

evidence: UT Plant Resources Center provides a Travis County herbarium specimen/index record.
Illinois herbarium portal exposes exact Travis and Uvalde specimens under Bernardia myricifolia/myricaefolia.
Bear Bluff Ranch botanical survey explicitly records Bernardia myricifolia in Medina County.
target_zone_range.guardrail: PASS uses exact county records; no statewide/ecoregion inference.

diagnostics: leaf blades broadly elliptic to orbiculate with revolute crenate margins
abaxial leaf surface grayish-white and densely stellate-pubescent with prominent veins
caducous green-to-straw stipules lacking dark resinous exudate
dioecious reproductive presentation; staminate thyrses 5–15 mm
3-carpellate pistil with three styles densely penicillate adaxially

lookalikes.separator: B. incana has persistent darkened/thickened stipule bases with resinous exudate and usually only 5–7 stamens; B. myricifolia has caducous non-resinous stipules and usually 12–15 stamens.
B. obovata has greener, sparsely stellate-pubescent abaxial leaf surfaces and a 2-carpellate pistil; B. myricifolia is densely gray-white beneath and 3-carpellate.
Do not rely on stellate hairs alone; confirm Bernardia reproductive architecture and 3-lobed capsule.

photos.assessment: Existing NPSOT habit/leaf lead is useful, but learner-complete imagery should separately lock abaxial stellate pubescence, male flowers/thyrse, female flower/styles, and mature 3-lobed capsule. Current leads do not yet prove every diagnostic role.
